The maintainer's rule: the OpenAI Codex CLI must not be installed on work-mac
OR ANY OTHER work profile. Your PR only disables it in
`home/identities/work-mac.nix`, so `paflynn@bushmills` and `paflynn@crostini`
(which use `home/identities/work.nix` directly, see `flake.nix`
homeConfigurations) would still get codex. Fix that on the existing PR branch.

## Exact change

1. `home/identities/work.nix` (the shared work identity; `work-mac.nix`
   imports it): add

   ```nix
   # Codex is not permitted on work profiles (corp policy)
   cosmo.codex.enable = false;
   ```

   Place it near the existing `cosmo.klaus.pollFallback = true;` block. One
   terse comment line, no prose.

2. `home/identities/work-mac.nix`: revert your edits there entirely. Restore
   the original comment text ("Claude-code and Klaus are blacklisted on work
   macOS due to corporate policies") and remove the `cosmo.codex.enable = false;`
   line; the setting now flows in through the `./work.nix` import. The file
   must match `origin/main` byte for byte after this.

`home/dev.nix` stays as it is in the PR.


for that check, e.g.
`nix eval --raw '.#homeConfigurations."paflynn@bushmills".config.cosmo.codex.enable'`
should print `false` and the same for `paflynn@crostini` and
`paflynn@paflynn-mac`; `personal` and `patrick@crostini` print `true`.

DO NOT run anything in the background. DO NOT use Monitor or background
tasks. Run each verification in the FOREGROUND and wait. Do not park, do not
schedule a wakeup, do not exit before committing and pushing.

# Add the OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex`) to the Home Manager dev profile

## What and why

`home/dev.nix` is cosmo's Home Manager "dev profile": the layer every developer
host composes (`personal`, `paflynn@bushmills`, both crostini configs, and the
work macOS config `paflynn@paflynn-mac` via `home/identities/work-mac.nix`).
It already installs `claude-code`. Add the OpenAI Codex CLI alongside it so
`codex` is on PATH on dev hosts.

nixpkgs at cosmo's locked revision (`flake.lock` -> `d2f67949798825fe853f7c5d0492b8bf016d3f88`)
ships `pkgs.codex` 0.149.0: Apache-2.0 (NOT unfree, no allowUnfree needed),
`meta.mainProgram = "codex"`, platforms include x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin,
and the x86_64-linux build is in the binary cache. Use `pkgs.codex` from nixpkgs
directly; do not add an overlay, a flake input, or a forward-pin.

## Exact change

1. In `home/dev.nix`, add a per-tool enable option mirroring the existing
   `options.cosmo.antigravity.enable` block:

   ```nix
   options.cosmo.codex.enable = lib.mkOption {
     type = lib.types.bool;
     default = true;
     description = "Whether to install the OpenAI Codex CLI (pkgs.codex).";
   };
   ```

   Default true so every existing dev host picks it up without per-host edits.

2. In the same file's `config.home.packages` expression, add a new
   `++ lib.optionals config.cosmo.codex.enable [ codex ]` clause next to the
   existing `cosmo.klaus.enable` / `cosmo.antigravity.enable` clauses. Do NOT
   put `codex` inside the `cosmo.klaus.enable` list: codex is not a klaus
   dependency, and that list's semantics ("klaus and its dependencies") must
   stay accurate. Keep the one-line comment style used on neighbouring entries
   (e.g. `codex # OpenAI Codex CLI`).

3. In `home/identities/work-mac.nix`, set `cosmo.codex.enable = false;` next to
   the existing `cosmo.klaus.enable = false;` line. That file already documents
   that claude-code and klaus are blacklisted on the work MacBook by corporate
   policy; a third-party AI CLI from OpenAI falls under the same policy, so the
   work Mac must not get it. Extend the existing comment to say the blacklist
   covers codex too (one line, terse).

Nothing else changes. No `programs.codex` Home Manager module, no config files,
no shell aliases, no docs beyond the comment.

## Style constraints

- Code comments: extremely terse, high information density, no multi-line
  prose blocks. Match the density of the existing comments in `home/dev.nix`.
- 2-space indentation; run `nix fmt` before committing (nixfmt-tree is the
  flake formatter, and CI runs `nixfmt --check`).
- Follow the repo's `CLAUDE.md` for commit and PR messages: no Co-Authored-By
  lines, no mention of AI/LLM assistance, message focused on the change.
- Branch from `main`; never commit to `main`.

## Verification (ALL IN THE FOREGROUND)

Run these and make them pass before opening the PR:

```
nix fmt && git diff --exit-code          # formatting is clean
nix build .#homeConfigurations."personal".activationPackage --dry-run
nix build .#homeConfigurations."paflynn@bushmills".activationPackage --dry-run
nix build .#homeConfigurations."patrick@crostini".activationPackage --dry-run
```

Those are the CI matrix entries that include `home/dev.nix`. `--dry-run` only
evaluates and plans; do NOT run a real build or `home-manager switch`. The
dry-run output should list `codex-0.149.0` among the paths to be fetched (or
nothing, if already in the local store) and must not report an error.

DO NOT run anything in the background. DO NOT use Monitor or background tasks.
Run each verification in the FOREGROUND and wait for it. Do not park, do not
schedule a wakeup, do not exit before committing. If a dry-run is slow, keep
waiting; each one finishes in a few minutes at most. COMMIT AND OPEN THE PR
BEFORE YOU FINISH. Do not end this run until the PR exists and its description
states which dry-builds you ran and that they passed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `home/dev.nix` declares `cosmo.codex.enable` (default true) and installs
  `pkgs.codex` when it is set.
- `home/identities/work-mac.nix` sets `cosmo.codex.enable = false;` with the
  corporate-policy comment extended to cover it.
- `nix fmt` produces no diff; the three dry-builds above succeed.
- A PR against `main` with a short description of the change and the
  verification performed, following `CLAUDE.md` message rules.

# Correction for PR #794: codex must be off on EVERY work profile, not just work-mac

The maintainer's rule: the OpenAI Codex CLI must not be installed on work-mac
OR ANY OTHER work profile. Your PR only disables it in
`home/identities/work-mac.nix`, so `paflynn@bushmills` and `paflynn@crostini`
(which use `home/identities/work.nix` directly, see `flake.nix`
homeConfigurations) would still get codex. Fix that on the existing PR branch.

## Exact change

1. `home/identities/work.nix` (the shared work identity; `work-mac.nix`
   imports it): add

   ```nix
   # Codex is not permitted on work profiles (corp policy)
   cosmo.codex.enable = false;
   ```

   Place it near the existing `cosmo.klaus.pollFallback = true;` block. One
   terse comment line, no prose.

2. `home/identities/work-mac.nix`: revert your edits there entirely. Restore
   the original comment text ("Claude-code and Klaus are blacklisted on work
   macOS due to corporate policies") and remove the `cosmo.codex.enable = false;`
   line; the setting now flows in through the `./work.nix` import. The file
   must match `origin/main` byte for byte after this.

`home/dev.nix` stays as it is in the PR.

```
nix fmt && git diff --exit-code

nix build .#homeConfigurations."paflynn@crostini".activationPackage --dry-run
nix build .#homeConfigurations."personal".activationPackage --dry-run
```

`codex-*` store path, while `personal` still does. `nix eval` is also fine
for that check, e.g.
`nix eval --raw '.#homeConfigurations."paflynn@bushmills".config.cosmo.codex.enable'`
should print `false` and the same for `paflynn@crostini` and
`paflynn@paflynn-mac`; `personal` and `patrick@crostini` print `true`.

DO NOT run anything in the background. DO NOT use Monitor or background
tasks. Run each verification in the FOREGROUND and wait. Do not park, do not
schedule a wakeup, do not exit before committing and pushing.

- Commit on the PR's existing branch and push. Follow `CLAUDE.md`: no

- Update the PR description: the second summary bullet should say codex is
  disabled for all work profiles via `home/identities/work.nix`, and list the
  eval results above under Verification.
